newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent last trades 26 cents up at July expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent last trades 26 cents up at July expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures last traded 26 cents higher on Friday in modest volume at the expiry of the front month July contract, trader said.
Short-covering ahead of the expiry was the main support for values but activity was muted with most players having rolled over their positions well ahead of time, they said.
July Brent last traded at $17.70 a barrel, 15 cents off the high and five cents above the day's low. August finished at $17.78, seven cents above Thursay's settlement.
"After a frantic week, this has been a pretty dead day in comparison," one trader said. "It's really just been plays on the expiry."
With the NYMEX July crude options contract expiring today there was additional buying support in the market, said brokers.
July New York crude futures were 15 cents higher at $18.84.
Brokers looking ahead to Monday said they saw a fair number of IPE shorts causing a small uptick.

Brokers earlier were split into bulls and bears by an Iraqi statement that Baghdad had no interest in delaying renewed oil sales under the "oil-for-food" accord, but would not export more oil until an effective aid distribution plan was in place.
"We had a little rally, then a little dip," said one.
He said the Iraqi comments were interpreted by some brokers as indicating that Baghdad was not likely to pick a fight with the United Nations over permission to resume exports in June.
Others saw it bullishly -- and more straightforwardly -- as meaning less oil would be on the market in June.

IPE gas oil futures closed at the lows. Front month July settled 25 cents firmer at $162.75 a tonne, almost two dollars down from the session high of $164.50 achieved on the back of Brent firmness ahead of the expiry of the July front month.
